output.review_comment:
Two of the three changes are correct: removing `hours %= 24` (docstring: hours "not wrapped at 24") and padding minutes with `{mins:02d}` (docstring: "exactly two digits"). These fix test_exact_hour, test_hours_and_minutes and test_more_than_a_day.

The problem is `minutes = round(seconds / 60)`. The docstring says leftover seconds are "dropped, never rounded up, so 119 seconds is shown as one minute". With this change, 119 seconds shows as "2m". The only test that needs rounding is test_ninety_minute_session: 5399 s is 89.98 min, which truncates to "1h 29m", but the test expects "1h 30m". That test contradicts the documented spec (and the truncation tests test_leftover_seconds_dropped and test_under_a_minute). The PR quietly changed the behaviour to satisfy it, didn't update the docstring and has no description flagging the conflict. Python's `round()` also rounds halves to the nearest even number (90 s -> 2m, 150 s -> 2m), so timesheet totals would change unpredictably. That's a payroll-sensitive behaviour change.

Please keep `seconds // 60` with the padding and no-wrap fixes (9/10 tests pass). Then raise the 5399 -> "1h 30m" test with the teammate/HR, since it's probably a typo for 5400. If rounding really is wanted, it needs an explicit rule (e.g. round half up), an updated docstring and sign-off.
